text:
[LEXP.5.11.1] `great_circle(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2)` is the distance along the
surface of a sphere of radius $R$ between the point at latitude `lat1`, longitude
`lon1` and the point at latitude `lat2`, longitude `lon2`, as a `length` in
`meter` ([LUNI.4.1.2]). $R$ is the binary64 nearest 6 371 008.8 m, the mean
radius of the Earth. The engine must compute it by [LEXP.5.11.2]'s composition.

Each argument is a `Float` in degrees, an `Int` argument being converted to
`Float`; an `angle` argument ([LUNI.4.2]) is first converted to `degree` by its
unit. Latitude is in $[-90, 90]$, positive north; longitude is in $[-180, 180]$,
positive east. An argument outside its range gives NaN ([LEXP.5.11.3]). An
adapter that delivers longitudes from 0 to 360 should convert them to −180 to
180 before it asserts them.

The sphere is a model of the Earth. The result differs from the geodesic distance
on the WGS 84 ellipsoid by up to 0.6% of the distance. A distance that needs
more is computed by an adapter and asserted as a slot.
